=== file-001.md ===
The Lantern in the Window

I follow the lane where the tired light thins,
With leaves whispering softly beneath my shoes.
The roofs hold the last of the copper sky,
And smoke curls homeward from chimneys of blue.
A sparrow shivers under the hedge,
While dusk gathers close to the fields.
I carry the day like a warm, folded thread,
Past gates where the evening's quiet yields.
Then there it is—one lamp by the door,
Gold on the steps, bright through the pane.
My hand finds the latch, and the road is no more;
The house breathes my name, and I am home again.

=== file-001.md ===
The Way Home

At dusk I turn where copper maples lean,
And chimney smoke unthreads the fading blue.
The road remembers every step I've been,
And crickets stitch the quiet into gold.
A lantern blooms beside the garden gate,
Its amber welcome warming all the air.
The porch boards creak, as if they could not wait
To hear the familiar weight of someone there.
I carry leaves and twilight on my coat,
And hear one kettle singing through the hall.
The dark comes softly, like a whispered note,
Then home unfolds its windows, gold and small.

=== file-001.md ===
# Homeward at Dusk

The last gold leaves turn slowly in the lane,
A kettle of dusk steams over fields.
My footsteps gather warmth from rain,
While chimney smoke unspools its quiet shield.
The sparrows stitch the hedges into sleep,
And evening folds the hills in russet blue.
I carry all the miles I meant to keep,
Then hear the old door breathe, and know it's you.
A lamp blooms softly by the windowpane,
The floorboards answer underneath my feet.
Outside, the moon rinses the darkened rain;
Inside, my wandering heart comes home complete.

=== file-001.md ===
The Last Light Home

The road turns bronze beneath the sinking sun,
A cool wind gathers secrets from the trees,
Dry leaves go whispering where my footsteps run,
While chimney smoke drifts softly on the breeze.
The windows kindle, one by one, with gold,
A porch lamp blooms beside the waiting door,
The evening wraps its blue around the cold,
And familiar shadows stretch across the floor.
I hear the kettle murmur through the wall,
My coat remembers rain, my hands remember keys,
Then home receives me, quietest of all,
And night folds gently through the sleeping trees.

=== file-001.md ===
# The Last Mile

The streetlights bloom as daylight thins,
And copper leaves lift in the breeze.
My footsteps find the familiar stones,
Past quiet yards and darkening trees.
A chimney threads the violet sky,
While swallows gather, then are gone.
I carry dusk upon my coat,
And follow one lit window on.
The gate gives its familiar creak,
Warm bread and lamplight meet me there.
I set my wandering heart inside,
And leave the evening in the air.

=== file-001.md ===
# Home at the Wrong Hour

The bus coughs me out by the grocery store.
October is a wet sock on the street.
Leaves stick to my shoes like old receipts.
The sky has gone gray and chewed at the edges.
I carry cold in both hands.
A crow drops something black beside the curb.
My house waits, yellow and square and dumb.
The key misses twice, then grinds in.
Inside, the radiator knocks like a loose tooth.
Soup smells burnt, but it is mine.
Night leans its dirty forehead on the glass.
I sit down without taking off my coat.

=== file-001.md ===
# Returning Home, Somehow

The evening drops its orange peels on the street.
I walk home with leaves stuck to my bad shoe.
The sky is a tired bruise above the stores.
A cold bus coughs and leaves me with its smoke.
My keys knock around like loose little teeth.
The houses blink their windows, one by one.
I smell wet dirt, old soup, and somebody's fire.
A crow complains from the telephone wire.
The moon comes up, pale as a forgotten plate.
I push my door; it sticks, then gives a groan.
Inside, the lamp makes everything look sick.
I am home, and the night keeps falling in.

=== file-001.md ===
# Home Again

I came home when the evening was orange and gray.
My shoes were full of road and one small leaf.
The moon looked like a dented dinner plate.
I said, “Hello, house,” because nobody answered.
The porch had cold teeth under my feet.
Autumn dropped its trash all over the yard.
A crow coughed beside the mailbox.
I carried the smell of smoke in my coat.
The door stuck, then opened like a tired mouth.
Inside, the radiator made a bad little song.
I ate a sandwich that tasted mostly like bread.
Then home sat around me, and I sat back.

=== file-001.md ===
Back Home at the Fall Evening

The bus coughs and leaves me by the bent mailbox.
Home is a box with one tired yellow window.
The sky is purple like a bruise on old bread.
Leaves slap the sidewalk, wet and not graceful.
My shoe collects a brown leaf and a small stone.
I carry both because my hands have nothing.
The wind smells like smoke, mud, and cold pennies.
A dog barks at me, then forgets its job.
The porch light blinks like it has a bad idea.
I put my key in the door, but miss once.
Inside, the heater makes a loud metal complaint.
I am home, and the evening sits down badly.

=== file-001.md ===
Home by the Bad Light

The bus coughs me out by the grocery store.
Evening is a bruise smeared over the roofs.
Wet leaves stick to my shoes like old receipts.
My coat smells of rain, onions, and bus seat.
A crow drops something black beside the curb.
The moon hangs crooked, like a chipped plate.
I drag my tired face past the leaning fence.
The porch light buzzes with a dying insect.
Inside, the radiator clanks and spits.
My key misses twice, then scrapes the lock.
Home opens its mouth, warm and badly lit.
I step in, tracking November across the floor.

=== file-001.md ===
The House Again

I came back when the sky was a dirty lid.
Leaves slapped around like unpaid paper.
My shoes carried mud into the hall.
A crow made one bad noise over the road.
The trees stood there, mostly empty.
Dusk smelled of cold metal and wet socks.
The porch light blinked and did not help.
I found the key after dropping it twice.
Inside, the radiator coughed at the wall.
Dinner was a gray thing in a bowl.
I shut the door on October's loose scraps.
Home sat down beside me, and neither spoke.

=== file-001.md ===
# Returning Home

The bus coughs by the ditch at six.  
I drag my shoes through brown wet leaves.  
The evening smells like old cold soup.  
A crooked moon hangs over wires.  
My coat has one damp sleeve and two.  
The houses blink their yellow eyes.  
I carry groceries, mostly air.  
A dog complains behind a fence.  
The road is dark and poorly paved.  
I find my key beneath a receipt.  
The door sticks, then gives a groan.  
Inside, the heater clicks at nothing.

=== file-001.md ===
Back to the House

The evening was orange in an ordinary way.
I came home from somewhere with my shoes.
Leaves were on the sidewalk, being leaves.
One wet leaf stuck to my left foot.
The mailbox had nothing except a beetle.
I opened the door and it made a noise.
Inside, the lamp was already doing its lamp job.
I took off my coat and left it on the chair.
The kitchen smelled like old air and onion.
A clock said seven, though I did not ask.
Outside, autumn continued near the garbage can.
I sat down home, and the evening sat too.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Evening Return

The bus drops me beside the store at six.
The sky is a gray lid over the town.
Wet leaves stick to my shoes like old receipts.
I carry one bag and a damp orange scarf.
The houses look tired, including ours.
A gutter coughs water onto the pavement.
Somewhere a dog makes a bad, lonely sound.
I find the key, which is cold and unhelpful.
The door opens with its usual swollen scrape.
Inside, the heater smells faintly like dust.
I say "I'm home" to nobody in the hall.
Then I stand there, waiting for the room to care.

=== file-001.md ===
# Autumn Return

The bus leaves wet grit beside the curb.
I drag my coat through leaves like damp receipts.
The evening is a bruised bowl of gray.
Chimneys cough into the low, dirty sky.
My shoes make small failures on the pavement.
A crow drops something black near the fence.
The houses blink with yellow, tired squares.
I smell boiled cabbage, smoke, and rain.
The key sticks, then turns with a cheap click.
Inside, the radiator knocks for no good reason.
I put my cold hands under the bad light.
Home waits, ordinary as a stain.

=== file-001.md ===
Autumn Homecoming

I came home at evening, dragging one shoe,
While orange leaves coughed like old shampoo.
The sunset was gravy smeared over the sky,
A crow said "hello" and then forgot why.
My porch wore a jacket of damp, brown confetti,
The doorknob felt cold and emotionally sweaty.
I kicked through the season, kerplunk, crunch, crunch,
And smelled yesterday's socks preparing my lunch.
The moon rose round as a neglected pie,
My chimney made noises resembling "goodbye."
I entered; the hallway said, "You again?"
Then autumn fell asleep in a bucket of rain.

=== file-001.md ===
# Home Again, At Falltime

I came home when the evening was orange-ish and late,
My shoes made a soup sound beside the gate.
The leaves were like coupons, dead and unpaid,
They stuck to my coat in a damp little parade.
A crow yelled “welcome” or maybe “get lost,”
The moon looked boiled and emotionally crossed.
Smoke from the chimneys smelled mostly of sock,
While my key argued loudly with the lock.
I carried the sunset inside in a bag,
It leaked on the hallway and made colors sag.
Then home hugged me softly with furniture knees,
And autumn sneezed loudly into the trees.

=== file-001.md ===
# Homeward at Dusk

I came back home at autumn's evening time,
with leaves like brown receipts stuck to my shoe.
The orange sun was shaped like melted slime,
and wind went "whoo" because it had to do.
My house stood there, a box of damp old bread,
the chimney coughed a cloud of peppered gray.
I waved at one confused and crunchy thread,
then put my tired key inside the door-way.
The porch light blinked like someone's dying eye,
while pumpkins rotted into orange soup.
I said, "I'm home," and heard the fridge reply,
then fell asleep beneath a maple poop.

=== file-001.md ===
# Returning Home in October

The bus dropped me beside a pumpkin’s rotten grin,  
and dusk wore gravy-colored clouds upon its chin.  
Wet leaves applauded like old teeth beneath my shoe,  
while chimney smoke crawled backward, black and smelling blue.  
I hugged my leaking coat; the cold hugged harder still,  
a squirrel screamed my name from atop the window sill.  
The porch light blinked, then spat a jaundiced, buzzing flare,  
and something in the gutters combed its greasy hair.  
I turned the key; the door exhaled a cabbage breath,  
the hallway slurped my footsteps, damp and warm as death.  
At last I reached my room, where autumn’s shadows sprawled,  
and slept beneath the blanket while the ceiling softly bawled.

=== file-001.md ===
# Autumn Evening, Home Again

I came back home when the sunset looked like gravy.
The leaves went crunch-crunch under my shoe, navy.
A cold wind slapped my face with a wet old mitten,
While one orange leaf got in my mouth, unwritten.
The chimney coughed a cloud of dirty gray,
And my front door squeaked in a bureaucratic way.
I smelled burnt soup and socks from down the hall,
The porch light blinked like a tired eyeball.
Dear house, I missed your wallpaper's beige parade,
Your hallway rug that smelled like lemonade.
I hung my coat beside the autumn gloom,
Then tripped on a pumpkin and entered my room.

=== file-001.md ===
Home, Through the Rotting Light
I drag the dusk behind me, damp and black,
While leaves paste themselves against my shoes.
The gutter coughs up rain and bits of sack,
And every window stares without a view.
My coat smells faintly of the train’s old breath,
The wind picks grit and kneads it through my hair.
A bruised moon hangs like something close to death,
Above the houses sweating out despair.
At last I find the key, cold as a tooth,
The lock gives way; the hallway reeks of mold.
Inside, the pipes complain; the wallpaper peels.
Home folds its clammy hands around my throat.

=== file-001.md ===
# Evening Return

The street exhales wet leaves against my shoes,
Dusk drips from gutters, brown and cold as tea.
A dead moth clings like ash to the porch light;
The wind pushes its dirt beneath my sleeves.
My key finds the lock, then sticks in something soft—
A rotted leaf, or what I choose not to know.
Inside, the hallway smells of damp wool, drains,
And apples collapsing quietly in a bowl.
The radiator coughs up metal, dust, and heat;
A floorboard wakes beneath my careful weight.
I shut the door; the dark leans close behind,
While autumn scratches softly at the glass.

=== file-001.md ===
# The Walk Back

The dusk has brewed a metallic rain.
Dead leaves paste themselves to my shoes.
The gutters cough up a brownish foam.
A wind fingers the rot in the hedge.
My house waits, yellow-eyed and damp.
The key sticks like a tooth in its lock.
Inside, the hallway smells of wet wool.
The radiator clicks without warming.
Moths bruise themselves against the glass.
I hear something shifting upstairs.
I wipe the road's cold grit from my mouth.
The door shuts, and the night comes in.

=== file-001.md ===
Homeward in October

The dusk coughs rust through the gutters.
Wet leaves paste themselves to my shoes.
A dead crow swings beneath the telephone wire.
Smoke from chimneys stings like boiled hair.
The road sweats oil beneath a jaundiced sky.
Every porch light flickers, weak and moldy.
The windows stare back, blind with condensation.
At the gate, cold rain crawls down my collar.
The key grinds grit between its teeth.
Inside, the hallway smells of damp wool and old meat.
The radiator knocks like something trapped.
I step over a slug and call this home.

=== file-001.md ===
Returning Home in October

The gate coughs rust into my sleeve.
Wet leaves paste themselves to the steps.
A dead moth clogs the porch light.
The key turns through something soft.
Inside, the hallway smells of drains.
Cold wallpaper lifts its blistered skin.
Mud waits in the corners like old meat.
The radiator clicks without warming.
In the kitchen, a pear has collapsed.
Its brown juice darkens the floorboards.
Upstairs, the empty rooms breathe dust.
I shut the door, and hear it chewing.

=== file-001.md ===
# Coming Back at Dusk

The bus coughs black spit by the ditch.
I carry a bag that smells of wet pennies.
October hangs its brown socks from the sky.
Leaves paste themselves to my shoes like old receipts.
The streetlight blinks, then gives up, then blinks.
A crow drops something purple on the mailbox.
Home is the house with the crooked yellow tooth.
The key grinds grit into the lock.
Inside, the radiator clanks like a spoon in a pan.
My dinner waits, gray and sweating under foil.
I take off the day and leave it in the hall.
Night folds around the roof, badly but warm.

=== file-001.md ===
Home at the End of October

I come home under a bruised-up sky,
with leaves like wet receipts in the gutter.
The wind shoves a dead branch at my shoe
and coughs through the hedge's brown teeth.
My coat smells of bus seats and cold rain;
dusk hangs its gray dishwater in the street.
A crow drops something black beside the bin.
The porch light flickers, jaundiced and mean.
I fumble the key with fingers like sausages,
while the chimney leaks a crooked ribbon.
Inside, the radiator clanks without rhythm.
I step in, carrying the whole evening's mess.

=== file-001.md ===
# Back to the House Where the Leaves Goop

The evening wore its orange shirt inside out.
I came home with leaves stuck to my shoe like bad receipts.
The road coughed cars and a damp, brown smell.
My coat was a tired curtain with one cold button.
A crow yelled “welcome” from a crooked wire.
The sun fell down like a bruised cafeteria peach.
At the gate, the hinges complained in wet metal.
I fumbled the key, which felt like a small frozen tooth.
Inside, the hallway had the color of old dishwater.
The radiator clanked and swallowed a moth of dust.
I said, “I’m back,” to nobody and the soup.
Night pressed its thumbprint on the window until I slept.

=== file-001.md ===
# Home Again at Dusk

I drag my evening through the gutter's cold brown spit
The maples cough their rust onto my shoes.
A bent moon hangs like a dirty plate above the roofs,
and every chimney leaks a tired, crooked bruise.
The bus coughs me out beside the leaning fence,
where wet leaves paste themselves to everything.
My house squats there, its porch light blinking wrong,
a yellow tooth that cannot stop its twitching.
I turn the key; the lock chews back with grit.
Inside, the radiator wheezes like a drain.
I call the dark by names I do not mean,
then hang my coat, and let the bad night in.

=== file-001.md ===
# Coming Back in October

The bus spits me out beside a drain full of leaves.
I drag the day home in a bag that smells like pennies.
The sky is a bruised pan cooling over the roofs.
Wet branches scratch their black receipts on the light.
A dead moth sticks to my sleeve like a crumb of skin.
At the gate, one pumpkin sags in its own orange mess.
The porch bulb coughs, blinks, and shows me the dirt.
I turn my key through a lock furred with old rain.
Inside, the hallway breathes cabbage, dust, and socks.
My shoes leave two brown animals on the floor.
I call out; the house answers with a pipe's thick gulp.
I come in anyway, carrying the dark behind me.
